suggestions: Gate volume confirmation to non-negative correlation only: replace `Corr(volume,vwap,10)` with `Max(Corr(volume,vwap,20), 0)` (or multiply the trend leg by an indicator that Corr exceeds a small positive floor). When price rises but volume moves against VWAP, raw multiplication flips the composite sign and pushes those names into the wrong quintiles, which is a primary driver of the negative Q5–Q1 spread and weak long-leg contribution. Keeping only volume-synchronized trends preserves the institutional-participation story and yields a cleaner cross-sectional ordering from Q1 to Q5.

Replace short-horizon diff momentum with a smoother trend slope: use `Slope(vwap, 20) / Std(vwap, 20)` instead of `Diff(vwap,5)/Std(vwap,10)`. A 5-day VWAP change is dominated by single-day reversals and creates unstable daily ranks; a 20-day regression slope estimates persistent drift relative to volatility and aligns better with the volume-correlation window, producing more stable quintile separation and a positive long-short spread where both legs contribute.

Combine the three economic legs with a consensus rank operator instead of raw multiplication: form `Min(TsRank(Diff(vwap,20)/Std(vwap,20), 60), TsRank(Max(Corr(volume,vwap,20),0), 60), TsRank((close-open)/(high-low), 20))` (or a soft-min / geometric mean of the three TsRanks). Multiplication lets one extreme or mis-signed leg dominate or zero out the score, breaking monotonic bucket returns; requiring all three dimensions to rank high simultaneously ensures Q5 names truly exhibit trend + volume sync + close-in-range, tightening the Q5–Q1 spread and improving long-short Sharpe.
